afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 172227
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
327 PM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Drying and clearing conditions this evening through tonight
  behind a cold front with cool, slightly below normal, 
  temperatures expected remainder of the week. 

- Another weather system entering the region Friday will reinforce
  cool, below normal, temperatures entering the weekend and bring
  a slight chance for precipitation across the Arizona high
  terrain.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

A departing vort max, seen on water vapor satellite lifting
through NV & UT, continues to drive isolated to scattered showers
across portions of south-central AZ early this afternoon ahead of
its associated surface cold front. The cold front has slowed down
and is losing its distinctiveness, but dry air continues to 
filter in from the west. Dew points have dropped into the 30s 
across southeast CA and southwest AZ, with 30 degree dew points 
also starting to show up in western Maricopa County. Dry air will 
continue to push in through this evening and shower chances will 
come to an end while skies also clear up. The trough has dropped 
H5 heights down to 567-571dam across the local area and H8 
temperatures have fallen to +7-10C. This has resulted in 
temperatures only warming up into the upper-60s to lower-70s early
this afternoon across the lower deserts, which is a few degrees 
below normal.

Brief zonal flow is expected for Wednesday, which means little to
no change in H5 heights compared to now. As a result, high 
temperatures tomorrow will be very similar today, around 3-6
degrees above normal, but morning temperatures will be much 
cooler, ~10F cooler than this morning, with strong radiational 
cooling and light winds. Low temperatures tomorrow morning will 
mostly be in the 40s to 50 degrees. Some higher elevation areas
and rural valleys will dip below 40. Portions of western Joshua
Tree NP are forecast to fall to 31-33 degrees. While the
temperature may fall below freezing, the duration and coverage of
freezing temperatures is expected to be limited. So, have elected
emphasize messaging over issuing a freeze product. In addition to
the temperatures, there will be light winds tomorrow and a mix of
sun and high clouds. Overall, it will be a cool and comfortable
Fall day.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/... 
Another pronounced trough with strong cyclonic flow will 
propagate into the western Conus from the East Pacific during the 
latter half of the week. However, trends in both operational and 
ensemble members suggest the main cold core and negative height 
anomalies even further north than previous iterations. This would 
place the jet streak only into far NW Arizona while a decaying 
cold front essentially loses definition crossing the coastal range
resulting in little to no forcing mechanisms into the forecast 
area. Not surprisingly, modest POPs in prior forecasts have mostly
been eliminated. However, forecast confidence is excellent that 
this trough passage will reinforce temperatures 3F-6F below normal
through the weekend, and potentially result in the first hard 
freeze of the season for some mid-elevation locations in Gila 
County and throughout Joshua Tree NP. Some frost would also be 
likely in the more rural, sheltered river valleys over the 
weekend. 

Substantial ensemble spread is maintained early next week in a 
pattern characterized by northern stream blocking, but a strong 
southern stream subtropical jet and progressive flow. GEFS members 
are increasingly trending towards a deepening wave tapping better 
quality moisture over the SW Conus early next week, while the CMC 
and EPS suites are far more disparate and trending towards a lower 
amplitude, less impactful system. NBM output seems to be weighted 
more towards the majority of the EPS/CMC idea with very low POPs 
centered only over higher terrain areas. However, given the strength 
of the current El Nino episode and intensity of the subtropical jet, 
a stronger and more significant weather disturbance cannot be 
discounted.  

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1740Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation concern during the TAF period will be the
presence of SHRA and TSRA over the region during the late
morning/early afternoon hours withe the expected passage of a cold
front around 1745Z. Operational impacts will be relatively
limited, but a brief window of MVFR VIS and CIGs cannot be ruled
out in conjunction with any heavier cells that come to fruition.
SE winds will quickly become W'rly as the main band of rainfall
pushes through. Outside of SHRA activity, the lowest CIGs will be
down around 5-7 kft, but those will lift and scatter out by
sunset. No major impacts expected through the rest of the period.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Breezy conditions will be the main aviation concern during the TAF
period. W'rly gusts around 20-25 kt will be common through mid-
afternoon at KIPL before speeds gradually relax heading into the
evening. Similar conditions can be expected at KBLH, but gusts
should subside earlier and be slightly weaker overall. Once cloud
cover associated with a passing system pushes east, clear skies
will be common throughout the rest of the period. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry air will continue to work east through the region through
tonight with any lingering showers in eastern districts coming to
an end this evening. Winds will also weaken across all areas this
evening. Minimum afternoon humidity levels will mostly fall into 
a 20-30% range in western districts and 30-50% across eastern 
districts through the rest of the week and weekend. This will 
follow good to excellent overnight recovery of 60-100%. Another 
weather system moving through the region Thursday and Friday will 
likely not produce much, if any rainfall, but will introduce 
another bout of gusty winds and reinforce cooler temperatures. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to water releases from the dam. 
Water releases remain around 3000 cfs. This will have the 
potential to flood farm fields and low water crossings along the 
river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...18
AVIATION...95/RW
FIRE WEATHER...18/Benedict 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero/Benedict
